fields.standfirst: Painters and photographers who made their name against the odds.
fields.description: A selection of women who worked at the highest level in their time: court portraitists, Baroque history painters, Impressionists and pioneers of photography.
fields.notes: A conceptual collection written for the Galerio demo, not a real-world exhibition. Works are from the Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access collection.

fields.standfirst: Rain, waves, storms and still ponds, from Edo to Norfolk.
fields.description: How different traditions picture water and weather: the printmakers of Edo, a Ming master of ink, and a sailor adrift in the Gulf Stream.
fields.notes: A conceptual collection written for the Galerio demo, not a real-world exhibition. Works are from the Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access collection.

fields.standfirst: The portrait as a universal act, from Moche potters to Parisian salons.
fields.description: Portraits in oil, stone, clay and brass from five continents, brought together to compare what different cultures choose to show of a face.
fields.notes: A conceptual collection written for the Galerio demo, not a real-world exhibition. Works are from the Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access collection.

fields.standfirst: Clay, cloth, glass and metal: the work of skilled hands.
fields.description: Objects whose beauty lies in the way they were made: celadon glaze, woven strips of silk, lost-wax brass, leaded glass and hand-knotted wool.
fields.notes: A conceptual collection written for the Galerio demo, not a real-world exhibition. Works are from the Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access collection.

fields.standfirst: Manuscripts and miniatures from Persia and India.
fields.description: Small paintings made for books and albums: a folio from the Shahnama, a Ragamala page and the intimate courtly scenes of 18th-century India.
fields.notes: A conceptual collection written for the Galerio demo, not a real-world exhibition. Works are from the Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access collection.

fields.standfirst: Candlelight, shadow and the Baroque art of chiaroscuro.
fields.description: Painters who built their pictures around a pool of light: Caravaggio and his followers, a Lorraine master of the candle, and the Dutch interior.
fields.notes: A conceptual collection written for the Galerio demo, not a real-world exhibition. Works are from the Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access collection.

fields.standfirst: Myth, scripture and a quiet moment at sea.
fields.description: Paintings that tell a story or hold a single charged moment: a legendary abduction, a queen who faints, a sailor adrift and a boy with a soap bubble.
fields.notes: A conceptual collection written for the Galerio demo, not a real-world exhibition. Works are from the Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access collection.

fields.standfirst: A horse fair, a sacred cat and a galloping rider.
fields.description: How artists in different times and places have looked at animals, from sacred Egyptian bronzes and Dogon riders to the scientific eye of Muybridge.
fields.notes: A conceptual collection written for the Galerio demo, not a real-world exhibition. Works are from the Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access collection.

fields.standfirst: Sculptors, potters and weavers working outside the painted surface.
fields.description: Painters who modelled in bronze or clay, and sculptors who cast, carved and joined: three dimensions, from a Degas dancer to a Benin plaque.
fields.notes: A conceptual collection written for the Galerio demo, not a real-world exhibition. Works are from the Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access collection.
